parallel.requirements: Recognized the full bootstrap task and all 18 requirement slugs, including engine repair, engine checks, game replay output files, determinism report, and per-requirement patch files.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent implemented five game-script requirements itself, committed those patches, then assigned the 13 physics C++ files to an AgentSwarm with one child per file.
parallel.implementation: The parent produced replay_io, physics_contract, sim_world, physics_system, and replay_runner changes, ran deterministic local replays, and delegated the C++ physics query-chain implementation to children.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivery was partial: five requirement_patches were committed, the physics child work was not closed into a complete set of requirement patches, and the retry still found CCPhysicsShapeQuery.cpp stubs.
parallel.verification: Local replays produced matching hashes before the physics swarm, but no post-swarm integrated build/check/replay closure completed; the official evaluator later saw three passing checks and the deterministic hash failure.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The active CCPhysicsShapeQuery child was aborted, the retry still saw hollowed stubs in that file, only five of 18 requirement patches were collected, and the final official outcome did not pass.

serial.requirements: Received the same full task and requirement set and continued from an 8/18 coverage state into the remaining ten slugs during round 3.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main agent kept ownership of all remaining work, sequencing C++ query modules, engine checks, game-script commits, replay execution, and output inspection without subagents.
serial.implementation: Serial implemented and committed physics_raycast, physics_spatial_index, physics_shape_query, physics_world_query, physics_debug_draw, physics_contract, replay_io, sim_world, physics_system, and replay_runner in the final round.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run reached a complete set of 18 requirement patch files and preserved direct commits for every requirement before official testing.
serial.verification: It built cocos2d-x, ran engine checks with zero reported failures, ran both headless replays, and inspected final state, matching hashes, events, and engine trace.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite broader coverage, the serial run still failed the current official deterministic-hash testcase and the pytest-session-tail case, so it was not a passing solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel prompt identified all 18 requirements and the full two-phase workflow, including engine repair/checks, game replay outputs, deterministic hashes, and per-requirement patch files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control received the same prompt and same 18 requirement list, so the task obligation set was equivalent across modes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement-set difference at prompt time; the later difference is execution coverage, where parallel closed at five patches while serial reached all eighteen patches.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel first implemented the five game-script requirements in the parent, then delegated 13 separate physics .cpp files to a single AgentSwarm with one child per file.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked in one main-agent sequence, carrying a todo list through remaining C++ physics files, build checks, game-script requirements, replay execution, and output inspection.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split the physics work across children and depended on a swarm result, while serial kept ownership local and advanced requirement commits one by one.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel child brief for agent-10 explicitly named CCPhysicsShapeQuery.cpp and enumerated the required shape-level query methods and Chipmunk APIs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial handled the same CCPhysicsShapeQuery scope directly in the main context, writing and amending the file before committing its requirement patch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The key gap was not missing context in the brief; it was that the active child carrying that context was interrupted before completing the work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented and committed the Python/game side first, ran deterministic local replays, then attempted C++ physics in child workers; the retry still observed CCPhysicsShapeQuery.cpp hollowed stubs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented the remaining C++ query modules, including CCPhysicsShapeQuery.cpp, then added game-script requirements and replay runner code.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial materially advanced the missing C++ physics implementation path that parallel left incomplete after the child abort.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received a swarm result reporting 12 completed children and one aborted child, with agent-10 explicitly interrupted and the parent prompt aborted immediately after the result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join; its main-agent work was directly committed and then used in subsequent build/check/replay steps.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a failed child lifecycle for one required physics file, while serial avoided a child-result boundary and carried the same work through local commit and verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The official harness repeatedly collected only five requirement patch files from the parallel workspace despite the physics swarm activity.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial harness collected eight patches after earlier rounds and then all 18 requirement patches after the final round.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial delivered the per-requirement patch artifacts for all task requirements, while parallel delivered only the five game-side patch artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran two local replays and saw matching local hashes before delegating the C++ physics swarm, but it never reached post-swarm integrated acceptance before the retry failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built cocos2d-x, ran engine checks successfully, ran both replays, inspected final state/hash/events/trace, and still failed the official deterministic-hash test.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verification happened after the C++ work and covered more of the full pipeline; parallel verification was front-loaded before the unfinished physics swarm lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out in round 1 after the swarm returned an aborted child, then round 2 spent its remaining attempt on current-state inspection before repeated provider 429 retries ended the prompt failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial consumed three timed rounds but used them to continue serial implementation through all requirements before timeout after replay/output inspection.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel budget closure cut across a live child and a failed retry, whereas serial budget closure happened after materially more implementation and verification had been completed.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records mark both modes as failed, so the official outcome is not discordant. The meaningful task-solving difference is that parallel stopped with five requirement patches and an aborted CCPhysicsShapeQuery child, while serial continued to commit all 18 requirements, build, run engine checks, run both replays, and inspect outputs before failing the same deterministic-hash evaluator case.
parallel_contributors: A 13-child physics swarm had one active child, agent-10 for CCPhysicsShapeQuery.cpp, explicitly aborted before completion.
The retry began from only 5/18 requirement coverage and still observed hollowed CCPhysicsShapeQuery.cpp stubs before 429 failures ended the run.
serial_contributors: The serial control kept implementation ownership in one main trajectory and committed physics_shape_query plus the other remaining requirement patches.
Serial ran engine checks and both replay executions after completing the C++ and game-script work.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both final official result files report the same passed and failed testcase names, including failure of replay_runner/test_outputs.py::test_hashes_are_deterministic.
The remaining deterministic-hash failure is not uniquely explained by the retained parallel coordination pattern because serial also failed it after broader task coverage.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference: the retained parallel pattern is an adverse process difference, not an explanation for a discordant official result.
